Founded in 2012, Cambridge Hospital has spent over thirteen years building what no other provider in the Gulf has matched: a fully integrated, dual-accredited clinical network that supports patients from the first day of post-acute care through to long-term management, community reintegration, and home-based support. Across more than 715 beds and six purpose-built facilities, our multidisciplinary teams deliver outcome-driven care to patients with complex neurological conditions, long-term ventilation dependency, post-surgical rehabilitation needs, and medically complex profiles requiring sustained clinical oversight. We do not treat conditions. We treat people, in the full context of their lives, their families, and their futures.

Cambridge Hospital continues to expand its services across the United Arab Emirates and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as part of Cambridge Health Group’s commitment to advancing rehabilitation and extended care in the region.

As the platform grows, the focus remains on expanding access to specialized care for patients requiring structured recovery pathways, long-term medical support, and multidisciplinary rehabilitation, addressing the increasing demand for post-acute and long-term care services across both markets. Cambridge Hospital is committed to delivering patient-centered care that enables individuals with serious injury or illness to achieve meaningful improvements in their quality of life, supported by a comprehensive range of rehabilitation services including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy, hydrotherapy, and respiratory care. Operating in alignment with internationally recognized standards, Cambridge Hospital maintains a strong commitment to quality and patient safety, ensuring consistency and excellence in care delivery across all locations. As Cambridge Hospital continues to evolve, the focus remains on strengthening its role as a regional provider of rehabilitation, post-acute care, and long-term care services, while maintaining a clear commitment to clinical excellence.
We are guided by a clear purpose, a strong vision, and values that shape every patient experience and clinical outcome.

We provide coordinated care across inpatient, outpatient, and home settings for every stage of recovery.

At Cambridge Hospital, our care model is built around one principle: recovery is not a single event, but a continuous journey. We provide coordinated care across inpatient rehabilitation services, outpatient care and home healthcare, ensuring each patient receives the right level of medical support, therapy and follow-up at every stage of recovery. Our multidisciplinary teams manage complex medical conditions, neurological injuries, pediatric needs, ventilated patient care and long-term recovery pathways through structured programs designed to restore function, improve independence and enhance quality of life. Whether a patient requires intensive inpatient support, specialist outpatient rehabilitation or rehabilitation at home, Cambridge Hospital delivers care that is clinically focused, personalized and connected.

Our care pathways are designed to move with the patient. Many patients begin with inpatient rehabilitation, where medical supervision, therapy intensity and daily care coordination are essential. As recovery progresses, care can transition into outpatient rehabilitation or home healthcare services to maintain momentum, support functional gains and reduce avoidable readmissions. This integrated approach allows Cambridge Hospital to deliver post-acute care, long-term care, ventilator-related care, pediatric rehabilitation and therapy services within one connected system of care.

Accidents can cause serious physical and emotional trauma requiring immediate care. After emergency treatment, patients benefit from specialized rehabilitation to regain function and overcome challenges.

Rehabilitation, or rehab, is a special form of care that enables people who have suffered a traumatic event or injury to regain their regular bodily and mental function. People go into rehab for a variety of reasons, including to recover from drug abuse, restore their mental health, regain their physical function after a stroke or other brain injuries, or to recover from a serious accident. After an accident, the victim must get the medical attention they need, especially if they have experienced a serious personal injury. Some more serious examples of injury include traumatic brain injury (TBI), penetrating head injury, a harsh blow to the head that can lead to more tedious medical conditions, skull fractures, or any other kind of traumatic damage to the brain which compromises their brain functions. A rehabilitation hospital can provide suitable medical care to patients who have experienced such traumatic brain injuries, traumatic events, and more. First, the patient will be taken to the emergency room (ER) in a hospital and may have to undergo an emergency medical procedure, like surgery. After the patient regains consciousness, they will need professional help in learning how to regain the ability to perform regular tasks, like walking, eating, talking, and bathing. This is especially true for patients who have experienced brain injuries or broken bones, which put them in a mentally and physically compromised state, respectively. When this happens, it is important to seek a trained rehab center with professionals who can teach them how to regain full mind and body consciousness and become a functioning member of society once again.

Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is entrapment neuropathy that affects the Median nerve. This can cause sensory and motor function deficits in the hand. Occupational therapy has an essential role in helping people with CTS regain function and improve their quality of life.

At Cambridge Hospital, Carpal Tunnel Syndrome is managed through a comprehensive, patient-centered rehabilitation approach. We focus on addressing the root cause of symptoms while restoring hand function, reducing pain, and improving quality of life. Our multidisciplinary team, including physiatrists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and pain management specialists, works collaboratively to deliver personalized care tailored to each patient’s condition and lifestyle.

Every patient at Cambridge benefits from a tailored care plan that may include physiotherapy, occupational therapy, splinting, pain management strategies, and lifestyle modifications, ensuring a holistic and sustainable recovery journey.

Patient-Centered Care: We begin by understanding your symptoms, daily challenges, and goals to design a treatment plan that fits your life. Multidisciplinary Approach: Combining physiotherapy, occupational therapy, splinting, and medical management to ensure optimal recovery outcomes. Evidence-Based Treatment: Our interventions are guided by the latest clinical research and international rehabilitation standards. Function-Focused Rehabilitation: We prioritize restoring hand strength, mobility, and coordination to help you return to daily activities with confidence.

Accurate Assessment & Diagnosis A detailed clinical evaluation is conducted to identify the severity of nerve compression and functional limitations. Personalized Treatment Planning Each patient receives an individualized rehabilitation plan based on their symptoms, occupation, and lifestyle needs. Active Rehabilitation & Therapy Targeted therapies focus on reducing inflammation, relieving pressure on the median nerve, and improving hand function through guided exercises and techniques. Education & Prevention Patients are educated on posture, ergonomics, and activity modification to prevent symptom recurrence.

This syndrome is a form of a condition that can cause pain, numbness, and tingling in the thumb, middle finger, and half of the ring finger. A wrist fracture can reduce the tunnel area leading to non-healthy body alignment of the flexor tendons. It creates pressure on the median nerve, which runs from the shoulder to the hand. This pressure can result from repetitive motions, such as those often used in typing or sewing. This pressure can also result from swelling or inflammation in the tissues around the nerve. Carpal tunnel syndrome can cause pain, numbness, and tingling in the hands and wrists. Different psychosocial factors are also responsible for upper extremity disability. It can also lead to muscle weakness in the hands in some cases. Some common risk factors include rheumatoid arthritis, obesity, and pregnancy. Sensory examination is essential for patient satisfaction during the early stages.

Dr. Ahmad Al Khayer serves as Chief Executive Officer and Chair of Rehabilitation Medicine at Cambridge Medical & Rehabilitation Center (CMRC) in the United Arab Emirates, bringing more than 25 years of international clinical and healthcare leadership experience across the full continuum of care. A Consultant in Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine, Dr. Al Khayer completed his specialty training in the United Kingdom and pursued advanced fellowships in Pain Medicine and Spinal Disorders. He also holds postgraduate master's degrees in Orthopaedic Sciences and Business Administration, reflecting a strong integration of clinical expertise and executive leadership. His professional career spans the UAE, the United Kingdom, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the Republic of Ireland, and Syria, with a sustained focus on delivering high-quality, patient-centred rehabilitation and long-term care services. Throughout his leadership journey, Dr. Al Khayer has guided large-scale transformation initiatives, including service expansion governance development, and implementation of comprehensive quality and safety systems. These efforts have advanced specialised rehabilitation services, strengthened patient experience, and supported sustainable organisational performance. As CEO, he provides strategic oversight across CMRC UAE facilities, ensuring clinical excellence, operational performance, and long-term growth while fostering multidisciplinary collaboration aligned with international best practices. He remains committed to delivering compassionate, comprehensive, and outcomes-driven care for patients and their families.

Tell us how we can help…
Join a team shaping recovery, restoring lives, and redefining care across the region.
Be Part of a Purpose That Transforms Lives

At Cambridge Hospital, being part of the team means contributing to something greater, supporting patients through recovery journeys that restore independence, wellbeing, and quality of life. Across the United Arab Emirates and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, our teams work within a unified healthcare system built on collaboration, clinical excellence, and purpose-driven care.

We foster a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment where clinical expertise, compassion, and innovation come together to deliver meaningful patient outcomes. Every team member plays a role in shaping recovery journeys — from physicians and therapists to nursing teams and operational support functions.

- Nursing & Ventilator Care Units - Pediatric & Developmental Care - Case Management - Patient Experience - Customer Service - Admissions & Clinical Liaison - Business Development & Operations - Marketing & Communications - Facility Management Each function contributes to a unified model of care designed to support patients at every stage of recovery.
A collaborative culture where your contributions are valued and your growth is supported.
We are committed to building sustainable healthcare capabilities by investing in national talent across both markets.

United Arab Emirates Cambridge Hospital actively supports the development of Emirati healthcare professionals through structured training, academic partnerships, and career pathways. Our collaboration with institutions such as Fatima College of Health Sciences reflects our commitment to nurturing the next generation of nursing and healthcare talent in the UAE.

Kingdom of Saudi Arabia In Saudi Arabia, Cambridge Hospital continues to support national workforce development across its facilities in Dhahran, Al Khobar, and Jeddah. Through structured career pathways, clinical training, and integration into multidisciplinary teams, we contribute to strengthening local healthcare capabilities in alignment with national priorities.
At Cambridge Hospital, our people are at the heart of everything we do.
